cards.title: The contract this repo ships
items: ios-best-practices loads on every iOS edit and carries the architecture digest (references/ios-architecture.md)
ios-review writes a prioritized report where every finding cites the rule it breaks and shows the smallest fix
ios-port ports a React Native, web or UIKit screen to SwiftUI-as-code, tests first, with a PORTING.md

lints/.swiftlint.yml + lints/.swift-format are the machine-checkable half: force unwrapping, implicitly unwrapped optionals and untyped errors are opt-in rules, and scripts/check-lints.sh proves the clean control stays quiet while the violation harness fires

cards.title: The five targets
items: Domain is pure Swift: a SwiftUI import does not compile, and the target dependency list is the whole allow-list
Data owns the SDK, GRDB and Keychain adapters and never imports SwiftUI or a feature UI
UI owns the ViewModel, one closed state enum, intents, effects and the views — never another feature's internals
the app target is the composition root (AppEnvironment), the router and the DI wiring; it holds no business logic

cards.title: State and secrets
items: GRDB (SQLite/WAL) holds the cache and the outbox table; migrations are code-defined and tested against fixtures of every released version
the Keychain holds tokens and secrets with the right accessibility class — a token in UserDefaults is a breach on a shared device
UserDefaults carries non-sensitive preferences only, and the outbox is drained on reconnect, foreground and background task

cards.title: The server is authoritative
items: the client hides an action it cannot perform; it never decides access — authorization is server-side, and a route guard is not access control
App Attest is a server-side risk signal, never a client-side block; ATS stays on and pinning needs a rotation plan
push is a channel, not a data path: the payload is {v, type, id, route}, the tap goes through the same deep-link parser, and the app fetches the resource
